# local 0009: sdas8051 writes 00 as the opcode byte of ACALL and AJMP since r16924

- Category: [Trivial fixes](../../fix-trivial.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply the patch.
- Patch: [local-0009.patch](../../patches/local-0009.patch), commit [`4d56db3f6`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/4d56db3f6521e8df8b4a4e97c4e36abe3bdcbff0). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.

```diff
diff --git a/sdas/as8051/i51mch.c b/sdas/as8051/i51mch.c
index e49413266..bcbca25ba 100644
--- a/sdas/as8051/i51mch.c
+++ b/sdas/as8051/i51mch.c
@@ -105,7 +105,7 @@ machine(struct mne *mp)
 		 * Top 3 bits become the MSBs of the op-code.
 		 */
 		expr(&e);
-		outrwm(&e, R_J11, op << 8);
+		outrwm(&e, R_J11, op);
 		break;
 
 	case S_JMP16:
```

## Finding

On r17176, `sdas8051` assembles every `ACALL` and `AJMP` with the opcode byte 00. After linking,
the first byte of the instruction has the upper three bits of the 11-bit address and no opcode
bits. The file below links to `00 04 00 00 22`, and `11 04 01 00 22` is correct.

```
        .area   HOME (CODE)
start:
        acall   sub
        ajmp    start
sub:
        ret
```

It was assembled with `sdas8051 -l -o reloc.asm` and linked with `sdld -nf reloc.lk`. The command
file `reloc.lk` has the lines `-muwx`, `-i reloc.ihx`, `-M`, `reloc.rel`, an empty line, and `-e`.

Programs compiled with `--acall-ajmp` have the same defect. The program below was compiled with
`sdcc -mmcs51 --acall-ajmp aa.c`. In `aa.rst`, the listing that the linker writes, the
`ajmp __sdcc_gsinit_startup` at address 0 is `00 4C`, and `acall _main` is `00 AA`. In ucsim the
program counter is at 0x9741 after 3000 instructions, which is outside the program.

```c
unsigned char count;
void bump (void) { count++; }
void main (void)
{
  unsigned char i;
  for (i = 0; i < 5; i++)
    bump ();
  for (;;)
    ;
}
```

## Cause

Since [r16924](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/16924/), which has the log message "Initial
OPCY_* changes from upstream asxxxx", the call for these two instructions in `machine` in
`sdas/as8051/i51mch.c` is `outrwm(&e, R_J11, op << 8)`. Before, it was `outrwm(&e, R_J11, op)`.
`outrwm` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asout.c` takes the opcode itself as its third argument. It writes the
low byte of that argument to the T line after the two address bytes, and `sdld` merges that byte
with the upper three bits of the address. The low byte of `op << 8` is 00. The call for sdas390 in
`sdas/as8xcxxx/ds8mch.c` passes `op`, before and after r16924.

## Fix

`machine` passes `op` again.

## Verification

With the patch the first file links to `11 04 01 00 22`. `aa.rst` has `01 4C` and `11 AA`, and in
ucsim the program reaches its final loop with `count` at 5. Only the small model was run for the C
program.

`support/regression/tests/acall_ajmp.c` executes an `acall` to a subroutine and an `ajmp` over the
subroutine in inline assembly and checks that both were executed. Without the patch it fails for
the six mcs51 variants: the small, medium, large, and huge models, and `--stack-auto` with the
small and large models. With the patch it passes for them. On the host, stm8, and ucz80 the test
has no assertion. With this patch and the patches for bugs #3703 and #2970, the regression suite
for mcs51-small, stm8, and ucz80 and the diagnostics suite for mcs51 have no failure.

## Related

- The test of bug #3703 reads the opcode byte of an `acall` and needs this patch.
- The listing shows a cycle count of 12 for the `acall` and `ajmp` lines above, and the table in
  `i51mch.c` has 24 for both opcodes. `machine` takes the count from the table entry for the first
  byte that the listing shows, which is the high byte of the address. The listing in the text of
  bug #3703, from SDCC 4.3.0, shows 12 as well. This is the same with the patch.
